## 7160d1eda94b

**Reproduced defect: the generated distribution perfectly supports “keep the
component touching the bottom border,” although the intended rule is “keep the
uniquely lowest component.”**

I sampled seeds `910000..910299` with sample index `i*13` in each of easy,
medium, and hard. All 900 generations completed; all 900 had a unique lowest
component, and that winning component touched the bottom border in **900/900**
cases. See `checks/audit/7160d1eda94b/sampler_probe.json`. This makes border
touching a perfect shortcut on the measured generator distribution.

For an exact rule disagreement, canonical train pair 0 passes the target
validator (`validator_errors: []`) and contains a uniquely lowest component above
the bottom border. The supported Racket rule keeps that component; the rival
“keep only a component touching the bottom border” returns blank. The outputs
differ. Source-bound input, rule/generator hashes, actual output, rival output,
and command are in `checks/audit/7160d1eda94b/counterexample.json` and
`racket.json`.

The counterexample is lawful for the documented rule domain but was taken from
the canonical set, not from the current generator. The separate 900-draw probe
establishes that current generated cases exhibit the shortcut. No source was
changed because this was an audit-only target.
